metadata.note: Atlantic City Railroad (Reading system, South Jersey) 1889-1933 and its predecessor companies, each drawn under its own name and colour per Rule 4: Philadelphia & Atlantic City Ry/RR 1877-1888 (main line; Pleasantville - Somers Point 1880-1882), Camden, Gloucester & Mount Ephraim Ry 1874-1888, Williamstown RR 1875-1882, Philadelphia & Brigantine RR 1897-1903. Built from research/branches/atlantic_city_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-20), drawing only its drawable: spans. Ownership splits at 1 Apr 1889 (P&AC, CG&ME into the ACRR) and 30 Sep 1897 (Brigantine line to the Philadelphia & Brigantine); 1883/1884/1885 Reading stock control of the P&AC and CG&ME are NOT splits - the old companies kept running their own trains. Every ACRR feature ends in 1933: on 15 July 1933 the ACRR leased the West Jersey & Seashore and became the Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines (PRSL), a different operating company for this map. The PRSL's later service over ex-ACRR lines is mentioned in notes only and is NOT drawn in this layer. The ACRR main line here is the Reading route via Clementon and Pleasantville, distinct from the Camden & Atlantic / PRR / NJ Transit route via Haddonfield and Absecon drawn in pennsylvania_railroad_system.geojson and nj_transit_rail.geojson; the two ran side by side between Winslow Jct and Egg Harbor.
metadata.color_note: New colours chosen 2026-10-20, none previously used in data/: Atlantic City Railroad #1943A6, Philadelphia & Atlantic City #19A65F, Camden Gloucester & Mount Ephraim #732273, Williamstown RR #5F7311, Philadelphia & Brigantine #AF1DBF. READING-FAMILY QUESTION, flagged for a decision rather than settled here: the ACRR was a Reading subsidiary, and the Reading's own colour #2A6F97 (reading_main_line.geojson) is currently ALSO used by the Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines feature in pennsylvania_railroad_system.geojson. The ACRR was deliberately not given #2A6F97 so as not to deepen that ambiguity; if the project decides the ACRR should carry the Reading's colour (it was a Reading-controlled operating company with its own name), recolour all five ACRR features together.
not_drawn: Williamstown & Delaware River RR 1883-1888 (Williamstown - Glassboro - Mullica Hill): no source names a passenger train in those years.
ACRR Atco Branch (Atco - Williamstown Jct) after 1882: no ACRR passenger evidence (drawn only for the Williamstown RR, 1875-1882).
ACRR Sea Isle City Branch (Ocean City Jct - Sea Isle City): no confirmable ACRR passenger year.
ACRR Wildwood Branch (Wildwood Jct - Wildwood - Cold Spring Harbor, ex-Wildwood & Delaware Bay Short Line, ACRR control July 1930): no ACRR passenger evidence for 1930-33.
ACRR Stone Harbor Branch (Cape May Court House - Stone Harbor, ex-Stone Harbor RR, April 1932): no confirmable passenger year.
ACRR Baltic Avenue Branch, Atlantic City (1.1 mi street trackage): undated.
Ocean City RR 1897-1900, before the ACRR merger: operator not established.

All Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines years (15 July 1933 onward) on ex-ACRR lines - Clementon Branch to 1961/1965, Grenloch to c.1941, Cape May and Ocean City to 1981, Wildwood to 1958/1972: a separate company, for a PRSL layer.
Brigantine Transit Co island trolley (1893): separate electric street railway, not ACRR.
not_yet_sourced: Williamstown RR start [OPEN]: 1875 is the earliest confirmed year (1875 Official Guide via Fowler); passenger service from the Oct 1872 completion is likely but unproven.
ACRR Brigantine Branch start [OPEN]: 1891 is the first year the consolidated through line existed; the passenger opening (1890 or 1891) is not dated in any source in hand.

ACRR main east of Winslow Jct: the ICC abandonment (approved June 1933, effective 3 Dec 1933) is known only second-hand from a search summary of the sjrail.com wiki; whether any PRSL passenger train ran over it between 15 July and 3 Dec 1933 is unknown.

Cape May Branch: the 1893 (Fowler 1893 timetable) and 23 June 1894 (Tuckahoe - Cape May excursion) starts rest partly on two search-engine summaries; whether the Cape May RR / Seacoast RR ran their own trains before the 14 June 1901 merger (which would need a Rule 4 split) is unsettled.

Williamstown Branch: the Williamstown Jct - Glassboro passenger end is unknown; 1929 rests on Fowler's statement that Mullica Hill trains reversed at Glassboro, i.e. ran through from Williamstown Jct.
Ocean City Branch: opening date conflict (1897 vs c.1885) and pre-1901 operator unresolved.
Camden, Gloucester & Mount Ephraim traction 1874-1885 assumed steam; no source checked for animal or dummy operation on its street trackage.

Gloucester Branch mileage: Camden - Grenloch draws 11.8 mi against Fowler's 12.1 mi and Mt Ephraim - Grenloch 6.6 mi against Wikipedia's 7.19 mi; the remaining ~0.3-0.6 mi is unexplained (Grenloch station site not located; the documented figures may measure from a different junction).
Pleasantville - Somers Point mileage: 'approx 7 mi' is itself not sourced; 5.0 mi is drawn.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.

properties.company: Philadelphia and Atlantic City Railway / Philadelphia and Atlantic City Railroad
properties.line: Philadelphia and Atlantic City: Camden – Atlantic City
properties.speed_source: Estimate, unsourced: narrow-gauge steam road of 1877, assumed roughly 70 min for 55 mi on the fastest trains.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py on 2026-10-20
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap with opstrace.py, held to the Reading's own grade (ways tagged old_railway_operator=Reading / 'PRSL (Reading)'), not the parallel Camden & Atlantic (PRR, today's NJ Transit Atlantic City Line). Drawn 55.4 mi against 55.5-55.6 mi documented (Fowler; 1904 speed run Kaighn's Point - Atlantic City 55.5 mi; Wikipedia 54.67 mi at the 1877 final spike). Mileage by source, before simplification: Kaighn's Point - Winslow Jct 25.0 mi = 22.9 Reading-tagged + 2.0 untagged OSM rail (Kaighn's Point approach and South Camden) + 0.1 ex-PRR-tagged; Winslow Jct - Atlantic City 31.9 mi = 26.2 Reading-tagged + 0.45 untagged NJ Transit track into the Atlantic City terminal area + 0.0 on the C&A/PRR line. APPROXIMATED (straight) legs, 5.3 mi in all: Pleasantville - the Atlantic City meadows 2.4 mi (the Reading's lifted meadows crossing, bridged straight between its razed ends at -74.506 and -74.467); Egg Harbor - Pleasantville gaps 0.7 + 0.3 + 0.1 + 0.1 mi; five short gaps between Winslow Jct and Hammonton (0.34, 0.23, 0.21, 0.24, 0.43 mi) where OSM maps the lifted Reading grade in fragments beside the C&A; and a hand-placed 0.3-mi stub from the end of track to the Reading terminal at Atlantic & Arkansas Aves. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEATS: the line was 3 ft 6 in gauge until 5 Oct 1884 and is drawn on the later standard-gauge alignment as OSM records it; the Kaighn's Point approach is drawn on present-day track, not the pre-1914 terminal layout; the final 1.0 mi into Atlantic City is the Reading's grade as rebuilt and now used by NJ Transit.

segments.note: Philadelphia & Atlantic City Railway, 3 ft 6 in gauge: work began April 1877, final spike 7 July 1877, opened summer 1877, Kaighn's Point (Camden) - Haddon Heights - Clementon - Williamstown Jct - Winslow Jct - Hammonton - Egg Harbor - Pleasantville - Atlantic City. Receivership from 12 July 1878; sold to Central RR of NJ and Reading interests 20 Sept 1883 and renamed Philadelphia & Atlantic City RAILROAD 4 Dec 1883 - a stock change, the P&AC kept running its own trains. Regauged to standard gauge 5 Oct 1884. Dates per Wikipedia 'Atlantic City Railroad' and Fowler line 89/89B (narrow-gauge Excursion House spur in Atlantic City). Headway is an estimate, unsourced.

By source: 0.96 mi untagged OSM rail (Kaighn's Point approach), 0.75 mi Reading-tagged (incl. the abandoned 'Gloucester and Mt. Ephraim Branch' way), 0.5 mi through South Camden on track OSM tags as ex-PRR (the two companies' Gloucester lines shared this corridor; no separate CG&ME/Reading track is mapped there). The drawn line stops at the end of the mapped grade at -75.1215, 39.9035; the last ~0.2 mi into the Gloucester City terminal is NOT drawn because the terminal site was not located. The CG&ME was 3 ft gauge until 1885 and its Camden terminal was at Bulson St until trains moved to Kaighn's Point in 1885 (Fowler); the whole era is drawn from Kaighn's Point on the later standard-gauge alignment - a later alignment than 1874-1884.

segments.note: Camden, Gloucester & Mount Ephraim Ry (incorporated 17 June 1873), 3 ft gauge, opened Camden - Gloucester City 14 Feb 1874 via Gloucester Junction (Jefferson St) and Ship Yard. Reading control from mid-Nov 1884 (a stock change); standard gauge 1885, when trains also moved to Kaighn's Point (Fowler). Consolidated into the Atlantic City Railroad 1 April 1889. Assumed steam-worked from opening - nothing found shows animal traction; a source showing horses on the street trackage would trim this under Rule 5. Mode is commuter_rail because it was purely a Camden suburban line feeding the Philadelphia ferries. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.

segments.note: Atlantic City Railroad main line, Kaighn's Point (Camden) - Haddon Heights - Clementon - Williamstown Jct - Cedar Brook - Blue Anchor - Winslow Jct - Hammonton - Elwood - Egg Harbor - Brigantine Jct - Pleasantville - Atlantic City (Reading terminal, Atlantic & Arkansas Aves). Formed 1 April 1889 from the P&AC (consolidation agreement 29 March 1889); re-incorporated 14 June 1901. Camden terminal at Kaighn's Point throughout (rebuilt 1914). The ICC date is second-hand (search summary of the sjrail.com wiki). Headway is an estimate, unsourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap where the grade is mapped: Brigantine Jct (ACRR main) - Pomona (C&A crossing) - Oceanville - edge of the bay, 7.9 mi Reading-tagged plus 2.2 mi of gaps between mapped fragments bridged straight (0.59, 0.32, 0.05, 0.26, 0.22, 0.11, 0.70 mi). APPROXIMATED: the bay trestle and the island line to Brigantine Beach, 3.45 mi, a single straight leg from the end of mapped grade (-74.411, 39.445) to the centre of Brigantine city - the trestle landfall and the island terminal were not located, and the trestle was destroyed in 1903 so nothing survives to trace. 13.6 mi drawn against 13.9 mi documented (consolidated Pomona Beach + Brigantine Beach line, 27 Jan 1891).

segments.note: Brigantine Beach RR (inc. 7 Aug 1889) and Pomona Beach RR (inc. 21 Apr 1890), both leased to the ACRR 18 Aug 1890 and consolidated as one 13.9-mi line 27 Jan 1891: Brigantine Junction / Pomona - Oceanville - trestle across the bay - Brigantine Beach. Start drawn at 1891 [OPEN at the start]: 1891 is the first year the through line certainly existed; the opening of passenger service is not dated in any source in hand, and 1890 is NOT confirmed - do not move the start earlier without evidence. ACRR era ends when the lease was cancelled 30 Sept 1897 (Brigantine Beach RR foreclosed 27 June 1895, reincorporated 1 April 1896 as the Philadelphia & Brigantine, which then ran the line - separate feature pbrig-brigantine). Seasonal resort service; the Brigantine Transit Co island trolley (1893) is a separate electric operation, not drawn. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia "Atlantic City Railroad", Brigantine Railroads section (7 Aug 1889, 21 Apr 1890, 18 Aug 1890, 27 Jan 1891, 27 Jun 1895, 1 Apr 1896, 30 Sep 1897), as checked in research/branches/atlantic_city_railroad.txt. Passenger opening year NOT SOURCED (1891 is the earliest confirmed). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Atlantic City Railroad: Cape May Branch (Winslow Jct – Tuckahoe)
properties.speed_source: Estimate, unsourced: seashore expresses over a straight Pine Barrens line.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py on 2026-10-20
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap on Reading-tagged track throughout (27.3 mi; Conrail Beesleys Point Secondary and its abandoned continuations). Winslow Jct - Tuckahoe - Cape May 53.7 mi drawn (with acrr-tuckahoe-cape-may) against 54.2 mi documented (Fowler line 93). No straight-line leg.

segments.note: Seacoast RR / ACRR line Winslow Jct - Newtonville - Richland - Grassy Pond (Milmay) - Estelle (Risley) - Tuckahoe. Start 1893: Fowler marks Tuckahoe, 'Grassy Pond 1893t' and 'Estelle 1893t' from an 1893 company timetable. Operator treated as the ACRR from opening (the Seacoast RR merged into the ACRR 14 June 1901); if a source shows the owning company ran its own trains before 1901 this would need a Rule 4 split. Ends 1933 as ACRR: passenger operation passed to the PRSL on 15 July 1933, which kept this ex-Reading line for Cape May and ran it until the last Cape May train 5 Oct 1981 (sjrail) - PRSL years NOT drawn here (separate company). Cape May Seashore Lines tourist trains on parts of it since 1996 are a separate tourist_rail company, also not drawn here. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler line 93 (1893 company timetable station names), sjrail.com timeline (5 Oct 1981 PRSL end, context) and american-rails.com PRSL history, as checked in research/branches/atlantic_city_railroad.txt. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Atlantic City Railroad: Cape May Branch (Tuckahoe – Cape May)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py on 2026-10-20
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap: 26.4 mi, 26.2 Reading-tagged (incl. the Cape May Seashore Lines / Winchester & Western track) + 0.2 untagged. No straight-line leg. The line ends at the present Cape May terminal track off Lafayette St; the ACRR's own Cape May station (Washington St) was not separately located.

segments.note: Cape May RR (reorganized Tuckahoe & Cape May Ry, inc. 19 Mar 1894) Tuckahoe - Woodbine Jct - Cape May Court House - Rio Grande - Wildwood Jct - Cape May, opened with an excursion Tuckahoe - Cape May on 23 June 1894; Rio Grande station 'built in 1894 by the Atlantic City Railroad', so the ACRR is treated as operator from opening (Cape May RR merged into the ACRR 14 June 1901). The 1894 date rests on two search-engine summaries (PRR chronology PDF and the Rio Grande station article) whose pages could not be opened. CONFLICT recorded: the Cape May Seashore Lines article's '1863 by the Tuckahoe & Cape May Railroad' is treated as a conflation with the West Jersey's Cape May & Millville date. Ends 1933 as ACRR: passenger operation passed to the PRSL on 15 July 1933, which kept this ex-Reading line for Cape May and ran it until the last Cape May train 5 Oct 1981 (sjrail) - PRSL years NOT drawn here (separate company). Cape May Seashore Lines tourist trains on parts of it since 1996 are a separate tourist_rail company, also not drawn here. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia "Rio Grande station (New Jersey)" (1894) and PRR chronology 1894 (prrths.com), both via search summary, plus sjrail.com timeline and american-rails.com, as checked in research/branches/atlantic_city_railroad.txt. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Atlantic City Railroad: Ocean City Branch
properties.speed_source: Estimate, unsourced: seashore branch with street-level running in Ocean City.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py on 2026-10-20
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap on Reading-tagged track (12.7 mi + 0.2 mi connector): Tuckahoe - Petersburg (Ocean City Jct / Sea Isle Jct) - Palermo - Crook Horn - Ocean City, 12.9 mi drawn against approx 12-13 mi documented (Fowler line 94). No straight-line leg. Ends at the end of mapped track at the north end of Ocean City; the street-level stops along the island (51st, 34th, 14th, 10th Sts) are covered only as far as OSM maps the grade.

segments.note: Ex-Ocean City RR, merged into the ACRR 14 June 1901: Tuckahoe - Petersburg - Palermo - Crook Horn - Ocean City. Starts 1901, the first year the ACRR certainly owned and ran it. Wikipedia contradicts itself on when the Ocean City RR opened (34th Street station 'built in 1897 by the Ocean City Railroad' vs an infobox 'c. 1885'), and who ran trains before 1901 is not established, so 1897-1900 is NOT drawn. Ends 1933 as ACRR: the PRSL took over 15 July 1933, kept this ex-Reading line and ran Ocean City trains to 15 Oct 1981 - PRSL years not drawn here (separate company). Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia "Ocean City 34th Street Station" (1897 vs c.1885 conflict; 1901), sjrail.com timeline (1958, 15 Oct 1981, context), Feb 1952 Official Guide PRR New York - Ocean City table (context), as checked in research/branches/atlantic_city_railroad.txt. Headway not sourced.
